grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; none of Rules A–F applies.
grade.summary: The submitted solution correctly proves that Mulan can guarantee victory exactly when θ=180°/n for an integer n≥2. Both directions are logically sound and sufficiently justified by Olympiad standards.
strengths: The sufficiency argument correctly uses the continuous range of the angle at the cut point to make both child triangles contain multiples of θ.
The descent from an angle mθ to either an immediate θ-angle or an angle (m−1)θ gives a valid finite strategy independent of Shan-Yu's choice.
The acute n=2 case is separately recognized and the interval is shown to contain 90°.
The necessity argument establishes the correct invariant: from a triangle with no angle congruent to 0 modulo θ, at least one child remains free of such angles after every cut.
The algebra in both cases of the invariant argument correctly uses the assumption that 180° is not a multiple of θ.
